I wonder if there are 3 options for how a worker and AI could interact: (1) Embrace and leverage AI to become more productive and valuable in an AI-driven economy, (2) Ignore AI and hope for the best, (3) Seek a livelihood that is not negatively impacted by AI. Personally, I'm choosing option 1. That said, IMO, AI is similar to every other tool that humans have invented to be more productive. Some tasks get eliminated, some tasks become more valuable and other, new, even more valuable tasks become possible. The question in my mind is whether through adoption of AI the average task will require ever greater intelligence (not education). And does this then mean that an ever growing percentage of workers become less and less valuable? What does the data show us on this matter?
